name: vector.h
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable: the repo has only vector.h, demo.c, Makefile and a README with usage text, no benchmark files and no open issues; web searches found no shootout or post benchmarking it against std::vector or std::list.

name: Wagyu
listed_description: A general library for geometry operations of union, intersections, difference, and xor.
reason: Directional claim only. bench/ holds Google Benchmark fixtures (angus.cpp, fixtures.hpp, run.cpp) pitting Wagyu against Angus Clipper, but no results are published; README, docs, PR #20 and issues #31 and #85 contain no timings; node-mapnik CHANGELOG 3.6.0 says Wagyu is 'faster and results in more robust results than the previous implementation based off the clipper' with no numbers. Not benchmarked against CGAL anywhere found.

name: xdr
listed_description: External Data Representation; a standard for data serialization. Standard (no license applicable).
reason: A standard (RFC 4506), not a project: no repo, no code, no performance claim. Wikipedia was blocked by the egress proxy, so the page could not be opened, but a standard has no benchmark of its own. Only numbers found are for other implementations (a Go XDR library in Go serialization benchmarks), which are separate projects.

name: zpl
listed_description: C99 cross-platform header-only library with many goodies.
reason: Directional only. README has no benchmarks; CHANGELOG mentions 'hashtable performance improvements' (15.0.1), 'Performance improvements for JSON5 parser' (6.8.1) and 'Optimize zpl_strlen' (12.0.1) with no numbers; web searches for its JSON5 parser or hashing in a shootout found nothing.

name: ZXing
listed_description: An open-source, multi-format 1D/2D barcode image processing library implemented in Java, with ports to other languages.
reason: The Java repo carries no benchmarks and is in maintenance mode; it makes no speed claim. Numeric comparisons found only in search snippets of Dynamsoft vendor blogs (dynamsoft.com blocked by egress) cover zxing-cpp and Python wrappers, a different project, and compare against the vendor's own product, with ZXing slower, not faster. No numbers against a baseline in which ZXing wins.
